title: A Shallow Convolutional Neural Network Predicts Prognosis of Lung Cancer Patients in Multi-Institutional CT-Image Data
summary: LungNet uses pretreatment CT images to predict non-small-cell lung cancer survival across four medical-center cohorts, with concordance indices of 0.58–0.62. Transfer learning improved nodule-classification AUC from 0.82 to 0.85; these retrospective predictions do not demonstrate improved clinical outcomes.
ai_technology: LungNet, a shallow three-dimensional convolutional neural network with transfer learning
organization: Stanford University; Charité – Universitätsmedizin Berlin; Moffitt Cancer Center; Stanford University Medical Center

evidence.tested: Four independent NSCLC survival cohorts (n=129, 185, 311, 84) had C-indices 0.62, 0.62, 0.62, and 0.58; transfer learning reached AUC 0.85 for nodule malignancy classification versus 0.82 from scratch.
evidence.unknown: All evidence is retrospective prediction; the study does not show improved patient outcomes or clinical utility.
evidence.ai_role: A shallow 3D CNN extracts prognostic features from pretreatment CT scans and predicts survival; transfer learning applies the model to nodule malignancy classification.

source_review.scope: Primary full-text Methods and Results; bibliographic date and exact-result catalog comparison checked.
